rows.ts_value: Rate options are Term SOFR (1/3/6 months), Index Rate (one-month Term SOFR reset monthly) and Base Rate. Base Rate is the highest of Truist prime, Federal Funds rate +0.50%, Index Rate +1.00% and the Floor. All indexes have a 0.00% floor. No credit spread adjustment.
rows.ts_quote: all indexes (including, for the avoidance of doubt, Term SOFR and the Index Rate) shall be subject to a floor of 0.00% per annum (the "Floor").

rows.ca_value: Borrowings may be Term SOFR, Index Rate or Base Rate Loans. Base Rate is the greatest of the Agent's (Truist) Prime Rate, Federal Funds Effective Rate +0.50%, Index Rate +1.0% and the Floor. Index Rate is the Term SOFR Index Rate (one-month, reset monthly). The Floor is 0.00% and applies to Term SOFR and the Index Rate. No credit spread adjustment.
rows.ca_quote: "Base Rate" means, for any day, a rate per annum equal to the greatest of (a) the Prime Rate in effect on such day, (b) the Federal Funds Effective Rate in effect on such day plus 0.50%, and (c) the sum of 1.0% plus the Index Rate in effect on such day
rows.ca_location: Section 1.01 definitions: "Base Rate" PDF p.12; "Floor" PDF p.28; "Index Rate" PDF p.30; "Term SOFR"/"Term SOFR Index Rate" PDF p.46; Section 2.02(b) PDF p.52
rows.explanation: The benchmarks, Base Rate components, 0.00% floor and absence of a CSA all match. The only differences are drafting: 'Federal Funds Effective Rate' vs 'Federal Funds rate', and the floor sits in the 'Index Rate' definition rather than 'Term SOFR Index Rate'.

Initial pricing is Category 4 (SOFR 1.25% / Base Rate 0.25% / commitment fee 0.20%) until financials for the first fiscal quarter after Closing are delivered. Category 1 applies while a compliance certificate is overdue. Section 2.18(f) allows a retroactive true-up for inaccurate financials.

The CA adds an initial Category 4 level, a Category 1 default-pricing step-up for late certificates and a true-up for inaccurate financials, none of which the TS specifies. rows.attribute: Letter of credit participation fee and fronting fee
rows.ts_value: LC participation fee equal to the SOFR Applicable Margin on average daily LC exposure, shared ratably among non-defaulting Lenders and paid quarterly in arrears. Fronting fee of 0.125% p.a. on each Issuing Bank's LC exposure, quarterly in arrears. Plus the issuer's 'customary and reasonable issuance and administration fee'.
rows.ts_quote: A fronting fee in an amount equal to 0.125% per annum on the average daily amount of the portion of the Letter of Credit exposure attributable to Letters of Credit issued by the applicable Issuing Bank.

rows.ca_value: Participation fee at the Applicable Rate for SOFR Revolving Loans on the average daily LC Exposure, excluding unreimbursed LC Disbursements. Fronting fee of 0.125% p.a. on LC Exposure for each Issuing Bank's LCs, also excluding unreimbursed LC Disbursements, plus each Issuing Bank's 'standard fees' for issuance, amendment, renewal or extension and for processing drawings (payable within 10 days after demand). Payable quarterly in arrears on a 360-day basis.
rows.ca_quote: to each Issuing Bank a fronting fee, which shall accrue at the rate of 0.125% per annum on the average daily amount of the portion of the LC Exposure attributable to Letters of Credit issued by such Issuing Bank
rows.ca_location: Section 2.12(b), PDF p.65
rows.explanation: The participation fee (equal to the SOFR margin) and the 0.125% fronting fee rates match. The mechanics differ slightly in both directions. Both fee bases in the CA exclude unreimbursed LC Disbursements, which favours the borrower; those amounts bear interest instead. The issuer fees become 'standard fees' for issuance, amendment, renewal, extension and drawings, not the TS's 'customary and reasonable issuance and administration fee', which favours the issuer. The row is downgraded from match to minor drafting.

rows.attribute: Financial covenants (type, level, step-ups, testing, cure rights)
rows.ts_value: Quarterly maximum Consolidated Total Net Leverage Ratio of 4.50:1.00 (total debt less unrestricted cash, over Adj. Consolidated EBITDA). 'Covenant holiday' step-up to 5.00:1.00 for the four fiscal quarters after a Significant Acquisition (consideration over $100m, or related acquisitions over $100m in 12 months). Quarterly minimum Interest Coverage Ratio of 3.00:1.00 (TS typo '3.00:1.000'): LTM Adj. EBITDA over (total interest expense plus disqualified and preferred stock dividends). Pro forma effect is given to acquisitions, investments, dispositions and debt repayment. No equity cure.

rows.ca_value: Leverage Ratio (Consolidated Total Indebtedness net of non-Restricted Cash, over LTM Adj. Consolidated EBITDA) may not exceed 4.50:1.00, tested quarter-end on a pro forma basis. The Borrower may make a 'Step-Up Election' of +0.50x (to 5.00x) for the four quarters following a Significant Acquisition. This requires (i) a designation certificate at least 5 business days before consummation and (ii) written notice before the last day of the first step-up quarter. After a step-up, the ratio must revert to 4.50x for at least two consecutive quarters before another election. Interest Coverage Ratio must be at least 3.00:1.00 over 4 quarters. Its Consolidated Interest Expense includes dividends on Disqualified Stock and on Preferred Stock of subsidiaries only (Series A Preferred Stock is carved out of Disqualified Stock), and excludes amortization of financing fees. Pro forma investment and acquisition adjustments apply at the Borrower's sole discretion. No equity cure.

rows.attribute: Required lenders, voting and sacred rights
rows.ts_value: Required Lenders: more than 50% of loans and commitments. All or affected Lender consent is needed to: (i) extend or increase commitments or extend payment dates; (ii) reduce principal, rate (other than default rate) or fees; (iii) release all or substantially all Guarantors; (iv) release all or substantially all Collateral; (v) change voting percentages; (vi) change pro rata sharing of payments or commitment reductions; (vii) change the payment waterfall; (viii) subordinate the Agent's liens or the obligations.
rows.ts_quote: Amendments and waivers will require approval of Lenders holding more than 50% of the loans and commitments under the Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility (the "Required Lenders")
rows.ca_value: Required Lenders: more than 50% of Combined Credit Exposures and unused Commitments, excluding Defaulting Lenders. Sacred rights: increase of commitment (that lender); reduction of principal, rate or fees, with financial-covenant and default-interest changes not counting as reductions; postponement of maturity, payment or commitment expiry; s2.18(b)/(c) pro rata sharing of payments and waterfall; voting provisions; release of all or substantially all guarantors or collateral (each Lender); class protection. Pro rata commitment reductions (s2.08(c)) are not on the sacred-rights list. Subordination of Obligations or Liens requires each directly and adversely affected Lender, but (a) only before a bankruptcy EoD under s7.01(g)/(h), and (b) Lenders offered a reasonable opportunity to participate pro rata in the new debt are deemed not affected. The CA also lets the Borrower, Required Lenders and Agent amend any provision if non-consenting Lenders' commitments are terminated and they are paid in full, and it disenfranchises Defaulting Lenders.
rows.ca_quote: provided, that, only those Lenders that have not been provided a reasonable opportunity, as determined in good faith by the Borrower in consultation with the Administrative Agent, to participate on a pro rata basis on the same terms in any new loans or other Indebtedness
rows.ca_location: §1.01 'Required Lenders', PDF p.41; §9.02(b), PDF pp.119-120; §2.08(c), PDF p.62
rows.explanation: The Required Lender threshold and most sacred rights match in substance. Sacred right (viii), anti-subordination, is narrowed in two ways: it does not apply after a bankruptcy EoD, and the Borrower can avoid lender-by-lender consent by offering all Lenders pro rata participation. This weakens the Serta-type protection the TS emphasised. Two further borrower-favourable gaps: the pro rata sharing protection covers only payments under s2.18(b)/(c), not commitment reductions (TS item (vi)), and the non-consenting lender payout mechanism lets Required Lenders override holdouts on any provision.

TS: an undated 13-page "Marketing Term Sheet" from Truist Securities, Inc. for a $1,000,000,000 Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility for Encompass Health Corporation. Pricing, fees and expenses are in Addendum I (PDF pp.10-13). It is marked "for discussion purposes only" and is not a commitment. Many terms (incremental, covenants, collateral, events of default) are set "substantially the same as the Precedent Credit Agreement" (the Sixth A&R Credit Agreement dated October 7, 2022, Barclays as agent). That precedent was not provided, so only the terms the TS states expressly could be reconciled.

CA: a new, standalone Credit Agreement dated as of March 9, 2026 (SEC Exhibit 10.1, 142 PDF pages) among Encompass Health Corporation, the Lenders, and Truist Bank as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent. It is not an amendment, and the Closing Date is March 9, 2026.

Limitations:
(1) The filed CA ends with signature pages and does not include the Schedules (e.g. Schedule 2.01 Commitments, Schedule 2.05 Existing Letters of Credit) or the Exhibits. Individual lender allocations and existing LCs could not be checked; only the $1bn aggregate stated in the body was confirmed.
(2) The TS pricing grid (p.10) and the CA spread grid (p.9) are garbled in the -layout text. On review, both pages were re-extracted with pdftotext -raw to stdout, and every tier and column was confirmed. The less-than-or-equal symbols are dropped in both extractions, and tier boundaries were read from context. The grid quotes are the cleanest contiguous fragments of the layout text.
(3) In the TS's two-column layout, section headings are out of line with their text (for example, the "Maturity Date:" heading sits beside the LC and swingline sublimit text). Quotes were chosen so they do not run across those heading labels.

Review results: all ts_quote and ca_quote values were checked mechanically against the text files (whitespace collapsed) and all were found verbatim. Page references were checked against the PDF PAGE markers. Changes made:
- A08 was downgraded from match to match_minor_drafting, because CA 2.09(a)(iii) adds a 7-day Swingline repayment that the TS does not have.
- A14 was downgraded from match to match_minor_drafting, because the LC fee bases exclude unreimbursed LC Disbursements and the issuer fees are drafted as 'standard fees'.
- A15 and A16 locations were completed.
- X01 was added for the $3,500 assignment fee, which the first pass had left unreconciled.

Other economic items in the TS (covenant basket step-ups, Available Amount starter of $1bn, Significant Acquisition threshold of $100m, financial covenant levels) belong to other attribute groups and were not reconciled here. Spot checks confirmed the CA Available Amount starter of $1,000,000,000 (PDF p.12) and the Significant Acquisition threshold of $100,000,000 (PDF p.43).

TS: Truist Securities, Inc. "Marketing Term Sheet" for a $1,000,000,000 Senior Secured Revolving Credit Facility for Encompass Health Corporation. It is undated, runs to 13 PDF pages including Addendum I (Pricing, Fees and Expenses), and says it is for discussion purposes only and is not a commitment. Many terms are stated as "substantially the same as the Precedent Credit Agreement" (the Sixth A&R Credit Agreement dated October 7, 2022, with Barclays as agent), and only specific changes from that agreement are spelled out (basket upsizes, Available Amount starter, covenant levels, CPs, assignment and voting terms). The text layout interleaves left-column headings with body text (e.g. PDF pp.2-3, 8), so some contiguous phrases are broken by heading words in the extraction.

CA: a new standalone Credit Agreement dated as of March 9, 2026 among Encompass Health Corporation, the Lenders, and Truist Bank as Administrative Agent and Collateral Agent. It was filed as Exhibit 10.1 and runs to 142 PDF pages. Printed page numbers are 5 lower than PDF page numbers in the body. It is not an amendment: it replaces the Barclays-agented Existing Credit Agreement, whose payoff is a closing condition. Signature pages are included (PDF pp.138-142).

Limitations:
(1) The CA text stops at the signature pages, so none of the Schedules (e.g. 1.01A, 2.01 Commitments, 3.04, 5.18 Post-Closing Obligations, 6.02, 6.06) or Exhibits are in the file.

(4) Benchmark/index successor rate, the incremental facility (Permitted Incremental Amount of the greater of $1.4bn and 100% LTM EBITDA), sublimits, pricing, fees, default interest and day-count belong to Group A and are not repeated here.
(5) Pro forma calculation, the Available Amount and the bridge debt exception are folded into B07/B08 rather than given X rows, because those checklist items cover them.
